clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old male with prior right canal wall down tympanoplasty for cholesteatoma in 1966 presented with 2 months of refractory right-sided facial paralysis (House Brackmann VI) despite 10 days of intravenous medical therapy (cortisone, ceftriaxone, valacyclovir). MRI revealed recurrent cholesteatoma on the right side and facial nerve contrast enhancement with thickening proximal to the geniculate ganglion, initially interpreted as neuritis. Explorative parotid surgery with multiple biopsies showed no malignancy. The main stem of the facial nerve was subsequently resected. Histopathology of the resected facial nerve confirmed squamous cell carcinoma infiltrating the nerve, growing in minute nests and cords with morphology reminiscent of microcystic adnexal carcinoma but with pure squamoid differentiation. PET-CT staging showed no metastases or other primary tumors. Due to perineural tumor growth, radiochemotherapy was administered (total dose 66.6 Gy with concurrent cisplatin chemotherapy) rather than further surgical resection.
